target_customer: Institutional and later retail investors buying portfolios of short term real estate bridge loans; non-bank lenders as loan sellers
problem: Fix-and-flip bridge lending was a large non-bank market that was manual and hard for institutions to access.
business_model: investment manager charging fees on managed loan portfolios bought from lenders

exit.reason: Reported as a liquidity crunch and difficult rates environment; assets reported under a letter of intent

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly loan data workflow automation and investor portal; difficulty was compliance and credit selection.

defensibility.rationale: Lender relationships helped but capital and loan flow were contestable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Peers such as PeerStreet reportedly went bankrupt in June 2023 per one source; AlphaFlow wound down first.

market_need_then: Company cited a $75 billion fix-and-flip market; bridge lenders needed capital and investors wanted yield.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press coverage of funding and shutdown but no brand assets found; several unrelated AlphaFlow trademarks exist.

pivots.to: opened platform to smaller investors via Republic offering and TITAN platform
pivots.why: to broaden investor base; date approximate from Republic campaign page

outcome_analysis: AlphaFlow raised a $4.1M seed in 2017 and a $10M Series A in 2020, and reached about $800M in cumulative loan volume per one source. Rising rates and a liquidity crunch in 2022 hit short term real estate lending, its site went offline in late 2022, and assets were reported under a letter of intent in February 2023. A securities offering reportedly never closed.
notes: Seed 2017 amount and investors seen only in Crowdfund Insider and a mirror; fetch blocked (403). Shutdown article fetch blocked; details come from search summaries. Series A investor list from Davis Polk. Competition at 2016 not found in dated sources; later aggregators list Fundrise, RealtyMogul, PeerStreet. Date of Republic pivot approximate. Other co-founders not found.
